expectations.evidence: Document only mentions HEMLIG. Does not enumerate the Swedish classification levels BEGRÄNSAT HEMLIG or KVALIFICERAT HEMLIG anywhere.
Sakerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) is referenced prominently in the regulatory framework (section 2.1) and throughout the document.
FMV and MUST accreditation process is detailed in sections 2.2, 9.1, and the full accreditation roadmap in section 15.
Section 8.4 describes clearance verification against Sapo records, periodic re-verification, and immediate suspension on revocation. Section 3 principle 5 references Sapo clearance.
TEMPEST is covered in section 4.1 (SDIP-27 Level B, shielded room), section 2.2 (Tempestdokumentation), and accreditation roadmap (TEMPEST survey and testing).
Section 14.1 explicitly structures the team around 12 HEMLIG-cleared engineers with detailed role breakdown. Section 3 principle 10 references operational sustainability for 12 cleared engineers.
Section 2.3 explicitly states all data must remain within Swedish borders. Section 3 principle 4 reinforces Swedish data sovereignty. No foreign cloud services permitted.

Section 3 principle 1 states air-gap is absolute with no network path. Section 5.1 shows physical separation between zones. Section 10 details sneakernet/physical transfer processes. Not merely a firewall boundary.
Section 9.1 requires all cryptographic implementations to be approved by MUST for HEMLIG level. Section 3 principle 7 mandates MUST-approved algorithms. HSM must also be MUST-approved (section 9.2).

Section 10.1 details the sneakernet import process between unclassified and classified sides. Section 4.3 mentions hardware data diodes for one-way import. Import station (10.2) and staging area in network diagram address cross-domain flow.

While the document selects many open-source tools (RKE2, Gitea, Harbor, Flux CD, etc.), it never explicitly states a preference for FLOSS/open-source or discusses caveats around it (e.g., audit ability, support considerations).

Document references US-centric standards: DISA STIG (sections 6.1, 17), FIPS 140-2/3 (section 10.1), CIS Benchmark. RKE2 is recommended partly for DISA STIG compliance. While Swedish frameworks are primary, the reliance on US defense standards without noting Swedish equivalents or caveats is a US-centric assumption.
